questions.stem: What unit is commonly used to measure energy in food?
questions.explanation: Energy in food is measured in kilojoules (kJ) or kilocalories (kcal). 1 kcal = 4.184 kJ.

questions.stem: Which type of nutrient provides the most energy per gram?
questions.explanation: Lipids provide approximately 37 kJ per gram, compared to about 17 kJ per gram for carbohydrates and 17 kJ per gram for proteins.

questions.stem: What is meant by metabolic rate?

options.text: How quickly food passes through the gut
The rate at which the body uses energy (carries out chemical reactions)

questions.explanation: Metabolic rate is the rate at which all the chemical reactions in the body occur. It is influenced by age, sex, body size, muscle-to-fat ratio, and activity level.

questions.stem: Which factor does NOT affect a person's energy requirements?
questions.explanation: Eye colour has no effect on energy requirements. Energy needs depend on age, sex, body size, muscle mass, physical activity level, and whether pregnant or breastfeeding.

options.text: The maximum amount of energy the body can produce
The minimum amount of energy needed to keep the body functioning at rest

questions.explanation: BMR is the minimum amount of energy the body needs at rest to maintain essential functions such as breathing, heartbeat, and maintaining body temperature.

questions.stem: Why do teenagers generally need more energy than older adults?

options.text: They are still growing and tend to be more physically active

questions.explanation: Teenagers require more energy because they are still growing (building new cells and tissues) and tend to be more physically active than older adults, who have lower metabolic rates.

questions.stem: How can the energy content of food be measured experimentally?

options.text: By burning the food and measuring the temperature rise of water
By dissolving the food in acid

questions.explanation: A calorimetry experiment involves burning a known mass of food under a container of water and measuring the temperature rise. The energy transferred to the water can be calculated using Q = mc(delta)T.
